rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before dhāl in the same word, an unvowelled ṣād is brought toward zāy, its nearest voiced counterpart in place; speakers may also realize a full zāy.
rows.anchor: فالصاد الساكنة إذا كانت بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A moving ṣād is not replaced, though it may be approximated even at a distance; clearer articulation is preferable because approximation weakens the emphatic ṣād.
rows.anchor: تبدل لأنه قد وقع بينهما شيء فامتنع من الإبدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When unvowelled sīn occupies ṣād’s place, it shifts to zāy; unlike emphatic ṣād, it cannot preserve an emphatic quality through approximation.
rows.anchor: وكانت ساكنة لم يجز إلا الإبدال إذا أردت التقريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shīn and jīm can approach zāy because their articulation is nearby; examples include أشدق as أزدق and الأجدر as الأشدر, but neither becomes a full zāy.
rows.anchor: فالشين لأنها استطالت حتى خالطت أعلى الثنيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمس answers متى by locating an event in time, whereas كم asks for a duration or count; a time expression may be raised or made accusative according to its syntactic use.
rows.anchor: وأما متى فإنما تريد بها أن يوقت لك وقتا ولا تريد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When الليل والنهار والدهر والأبد serve as duration adverbs, they cover the whole named span; they cannot denote only one part, though extended usage can make them non-adverbial.
rows.anchor: قولك سير عليه الليل والنهار والدهر والأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Month names can denote a counted total of days, but شهر رمضان or شهر ذي الحجة names a specific time and answers متى.
rows.anchor: وصفر وجمادى وسائر أسماء الشهور إلى ذى الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Temporal and spatial adverbs parallel each other: كم can ask for counted duration or distance, while متى and أين identify a time and place; non-adverbial uses may be raised.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون أين إلا للأماكن

rows.speaker: ابن الرقاع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Riqāʿ’s verse with الشتاء illustrates seasonal expressions used as time answers; such expressions can also be understood as counted durations.
rows.anchor: وهو للذود أن يقسمن جار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun marks a required predicate after verbs such as ظن and distinguishes it from an adjective; Sībawayh cites the Qur’anic phrase هو الحق as an example.
rows.anchor: أوتوا العلم الذي أنزل إليك من ربك هو الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In رأيته إياه نفسه, إياه is an appositive and نفسه is descriptive emphasis; after the completed verb, قائما is a circumstantial accusative rather than a predicate complement.
rows.anchor: فأما نفسه حين قلت رأيته إياه نفسه فوصف بمنزلة هو وإياه بدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun and an emphatic pronoun such as إياه substitute for one another, so Sībawayh rejects combining both in the same predicate construction.
rows.anchor: ويدلك على أن الفصل كالصفة أنه لا يستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh says the separating pronoun is stronger with verbs than with إن and its sisters, where an intervening phrase can make إياك acceptable.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنها في الفعل أقوى منها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl accepts إنك إياك خير منه as Arabic, although Sībawayh regards it as remote; Sībawayh accepts إياك when an intervening phrase occurs.
rows.anchor: وكان الخليل يقول هى عربية إنك إياك خير منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An interrogative alif may follow waw, as in أو أهو; waw does not precede the alif as هل does, and this Qur’anic construction functions like فاء.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة الفاء في قوله تعالى

words: وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the negative command, أو connects the two objects under one prohibition; repeating لا after أو would change the meaning.
rows.anchor: لو قلت أو لا تطع كفورا انقلب المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an interrogative is repeated after أو, the question must be restarted; if the second question presents an alternative after uncertainty, أم is the appropriate disjunctive particle.
rows.anchor: ثم أعدت حرفا من هذه الحروف لم يحسن الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A question such as ألست أخانا أو صاحبنا may ask about a shared set of descriptions, while repeated لست clauses with أو can instead present alternatives.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلت ألست أخانا أو صاحبنا أو جليسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbs such as حسب and ظن take two objects when they report a certain or uncertain judgment: the first is judged, and the second states its condition.
rows.anchor: منعك أن تقتصر على أحد المفعولين ههنا أنك إنما أردت أن تبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رأيت and وجدت act like ordinary transitive verbs when they mean sensory seeing or finding, but can behave as mental verbs; علم can mean عرف and take one object.
rows.anchor: قد يكون علمت بمنزلة عرفت لا تريد إلا علم الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ظننت ذاك, خلت, and حسبت may stand alone because ذاك supplies the cognate notion of thinking; forms like خلت زيدا and أرى زيدا are not acceptable in this use.
rows.anchor: وأما ظننت ذاك فإنما جاز السكوت عليه لأنك قد تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ظننت به, باء is meaningful rather than redundant: it marks what is assigned to supposition, unlike the extra باء in كفى بالله.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت الباء زائدة بمنزلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In له صوت صوت حمار, the repeated noun is accusative by an implied action meaning يصوت; it is not an adjective or appositive to صوت.
rows.anchor: فإنما انتصب هذا لأنك مررت به فى حال تصويت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh compares this accusative to والشمس والقمر حسبانا: جاعل الليل implies جعل, so the following item is construed on the implied verb.
rows.anchor: فصار كأنه قال وجعل الليل سكنا وحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an explicit verb such as يصوت, the following accusative can give the sound’s model or be a circumstantial comparison; an implicit verb can also govern it.
rows.anchor: فإذا قلت مررت به فإذا هو يصوت صوت الحمار فعلى الفعل غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite sound noun can be construed as a simile with مثل understood; a definite noun cannot be a circumstantial accusative or modify an indefinite noun in the same way.
rows.anchor: فإذا أخرجت مثل قام المصدر النكرة مقام مثل لأنه مثله نكرة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl allows صوت الحمار to describe the indefinite صوت as a simile; Sībawayh calls the analogous construction رجل أخو زيد weak and restricted to poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل أنه يجوز له صوت صوت الحمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s repeated صريف exemplifies a sound noun after له; lines by Ruʾbah, al-ʿAjjāj, and Abū Kabīr show related accusatives explained through implied verbal action.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر وهو النابغة الذبيانى
